summary: Sheriff's deputies booked a 46-year-old man on a first-degree terrorist-threat charge and Gulf Shores police booked a 21-year-old man on a burglary charge, and Daphne police's updated arrest log now lists 12 solicitation arrests from Friday. The jail roster showed 17 criminal bookings dated Nov. 7 and one so far on Nov. 8.

entries.title: Terrorist-threat arrest: Gorden Ellis Wade
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Gorden Ellis Wade, 46, at 3:46 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6, according to the jail roster. He was booked Nov. 7 and released the same day, the roster shows.

He was booked on a charge of making a terrorist threat in the first degree — threatening violence to cause fear, evacuation or disruption. The sheriff's office had not posted a release about the arrest when its page was checked.

entries.title: Burglary arrest: Samuel Joseph Crocker
body: Gulf Shores police arrested Samuel Joseph Crocker, 21, at 4:56 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6, according to the jail roster. He was booked at the county jail Nov. 7 and was in custody when the roster was read early Sunday.
He was booked on a charge of burglary of a non-residence with no force — entering a building other than a home, without forcing entry, to commit a crime.

entries.title: Daphne solicitation arrests: 12 charged Nov. 6
body: Daphne police arrested 12 men on charges of solicitation for prostitution on Friday, Nov. 6, according to the department's arrest log as updated through early Sunday.

Five were arrested between 11:03 a.m. and 3:10 p.m. on Woodrow Lane: Jonathan Kirk Fender, Jayden Alexander Kelley, Jocquez Tyree Dixon, Jordan Ray Phillips and Joseph Dewayne Bates. Seven were arrested between 6:02 and 11:35 p.m. at the Microtel on U.S. 98: Diego Gaspar Mauro, Shannon Maurice Moore, Carlos Maurice Byther, Terrance Lamond Penn, Carlton De'aundre Eonte Lee, Juan Vellejo and Joseph Emmanuell Bailey.

An earlier version of the log, reported here Nov. 7, listed eight arrests and showed Byther, Lee and Vellejo as charged with prostitution. Daphne police had not posted a release about the arrests when the department's page was checked.

entries.title: Elder abuse arrest: Elisabeth Memphis Ingle
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Elisabeth Memphis Ingle, 37, at 7:47 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 7, according to the jail roster. She was released the same day, the roster shows.

She was booked on a charge of second-degree elder abuse and neglect — abusing or neglecting a person aged 60 or older. Deputies booked two men on the same charge the previous morning, one of them with the same last name; the roster does not say whether the arrests are connected.

entries.title: Protection-order arrests: Ricky Chandler Reed, Troy Anderson Brown
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Ricky Chandler Reed, 36, at 5:20 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 7, and Troy Anderson Brown, 33, at 8:40 a.m., according to the jail roster. Both were released the same day.
Each was booked on a charge of violating a domestic-violence protection order — breaking the terms of a court order protecting another person. The roster does not connect the two arrests.

entries.title: Firearm arrest: Michael Drew Robinson
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Michael Drew Robinson, 38, at 9:01 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 7, according to the jail roster. He was in custody when the roster was read early Sunday.

He was booked on a charge of being a drunk or drug addict in possession of a firearm — a gun charge for people the law bars because of alcohol or drug use — along with felony and misdemeanor failure-to-appear charges.

entries.title: Drugged-driving arrest: David Allen Lee Cooley
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested David Allen Lee Cooley, 38, on Saturday, Nov. 7, according to the jail roster. He was in custody when the roster was read early Sunday.

He was booked on charges of driving under the influence of a substance other than alcohol, unlawful possession of inhalants, reckless endangerment and probation violation, and on a charge the roster lists only as “Manufacture.”

entries.title: Bay Minette drug arrests: Ferrell Antonio Purdue Butler, Lee Baron Atchison
body: Bay Minette police arrested Ferrell Antonio Purdue Butler, 40, at 1:50 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 7, and Lee Baron Atchison, 33, at 7:14 p.m., according to the jail roster. Butler was released the same day; Atchison was in custody when the roster was read early Sunday.

Butler was booked on charges of cocaine possession, methamphetamine possession, buying or receiving stolen property and drug paraphernalia. Atchison was booked on charges of possessing a synthetic narcotic, tampering with physical evidence — destroying or hiding evidence — and drug paraphernalia.

entries.title: Identity theft arrest: Star Marie Amelotte
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Star Marie Amelotte, 34, on Saturday, Nov. 7, according to the jail roster. She was in custody when the roster was read early Sunday.
She was booked on a charge of identity theft — using another person's identifying information without permission.

entries.title: Attempting-to-elude arrest: Paul Ray Morris Jr.
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Paul Ray Morris Jr., 47, at 1:25 a.m. Sunday, Nov. 8, according to the jail roster. He was in custody when the roster was read.
He was booked on a charge of attempting to elude a law enforcement officer — fleeing from police after a signal to stop.

entries.title: Drug trafficking arrest: Arvia Lloyd Allen
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Arvia Lloyd Allen, 36, at 1:59 a.m. Friday, Nov. 6, according to the jail roster. He was in custody when the roster was read early Saturday.

He was booked on charges of drug trafficking — possessing or selling drugs in an amount the law treats as trafficking — and of being a drunk or drug addict in possession of a firearm, along with possession of dangerous drugs, marijuana possession and drug paraphernalia. The roster lists six charges in all. The sheriff's office had not posted a release about the arrest when its page was checked.

entries.title: Elder abuse arrests: Brandon James Ingle, Edward Arley Hale
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Brandon James Ingle, 38, at 8:35 a.m. Friday, Nov. 6, and Edward Arley Hale, 67, at 8:42 a.m., according to the jail roster. Both were in custody when the roster was read early Saturday.

Each was booked on a charge of second-degree elder abuse and neglect — abusing or neglecting a person aged 60 or older. The roster does not say whether the two arrests are connected, and the sheriff's office had not posted a release when its page was checked.

entries.title: Stolen-property and altered-firearm arrest: Damon Curtis Chisholm
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Damon Curtis Chisholm, 51, at 2:55 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6, according to the jail roster. He was in custody when the roster was read early Saturday.
He was booked on charges of buying or receiving stolen property, and of altering a firearm's identification or possessing an altered firearm — a gun with its serial number removed or changed.

entries.title: Drunk-driving arrests: Robert Glen Coats, Travis Jefferey Moran
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Robert Glen Coats, 68, at 4 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 5, on a charge the jail lists as driving under the influence of alcohol with three or more prior convictions, according to the jail roster. He was booked Friday and was in custody when the roster was read early Saturday.
State troopers arrested Travis Jefferey Moran, 38, at 9:02 a.m. Nov. 5 on a charge of driving under the influence of alcohol. He was booked and released Friday, Nov. 6, according to the roster.

entries.title: Attempting-to-elude arrests: Trevor O'Neal Lochrico, Justin Taylor Covington
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Trevor O'Neal Lochrico, 36, at 1:21 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 5, on two counts of shoplifting and a charge of attempting to elude police — fleeing from an officer who signals a stop — according to the jail roster.

Deputies arrested Justin Taylor Covington, 29, at 1 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6, on a charge of attempting to elude police. Both were booked Nov. 6 and were in custody when the roster was read early Saturday.

entries.title: Card fraud arrest: Danielle Zaneta Kennedy
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Danielle Zaneta Kennedy, 41, at 4:50 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6, according to the jail roster. She was in custody when the roster was read early Saturday.
She was booked on three counts of illegal possession or use of a credit or debit card — having or using someone else's card without permission.

entries.title: Family-harassment arrest: Julian Morales
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Julian Morales, 22, at 11:20 a.m. Friday, Nov. 6, according to the jail roster. He was in custody when the roster was read early Saturday.
He was booked on a charge of harassment of a family member — threatening, striking or alarming a household member.

entries.title: Bay Minette arrests: Caitlin Carol Reed, Ashton Harold Enrico Bradley, Madison Taylor Cubbage
body: Bay Minette police arrested Caitlin Carol Reed, 27, at 3:15 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6, according to the jail roster. She was booked on charges including drug paraphernalia, tampering with physical evidence, promoting prison contraband (drugs) — bringing drugs into a jail — harassment of a family member and failure to appear; the roster lists seven charges in all.

Bay Minette police also arrested Ashton Harold Enrico Bradley, 36, at 8:30 a.m. Nov. 6 on a charge of second-degree marijuana possession; he was released the same day. Madison Taylor Cubbage, 27, booked Nov. 6 with an arrest stamp of 1:48 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 7, faces an alias writ of arrest and failure-to-appear warrants, 14 charges in all. Reed and Cubbage were in custody when the roster was read.

entries.title: Federal sentences, bank fraud and identity theft: Vernon A. McCreath, Mikhail C. McCreath
body: Vernon A. McCreath, 39, of Jersey City, New Jersey, was sentenced to 192 months and Mikhail C. McCreath, 35, of Miami, to 140 months in federal prison for a nationwide bank fraud and identity theft scheme, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Alabama announced Nov. 6. Both had pleaded guilty.

According to the release, the scheme ran from 2015 to 2025, used stolen mail, counterfeit checks and stolen identities, and passed instruments at banks in the Southern District of Alabama, among other places. The Baldwin County Sheriff's Office was among the agencies the release says substantially assisted the investigation.
